speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information in light of the recent global cyber attack that forced Swedish Coop supermarkets to close, whether there have been any attempts to attack Singapore’s supply chain software in the past three years.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Coop used the Kaseya Virtual System Administrator (VSA), which is a software management platform designed to help organisations manage their IT services remotely.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Similar attacks have occurred in recent months, such as the SolarWinds breach reported in December 2020 and the attack on the Microsoft Exchange Server reported in January 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Essentially, they take advantage of unsuspecting companies’ introduction of new software into their systems that turn out to contain malicious elements or ransomware.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Usually, neither the companies nor their vendors that supplied the software were even aware that the software had been compromised.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The same software that was afflicting tens of thousands of organisations and businesses can also find its way into IT systems in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nevertheless, the Government continues to adopt a cautious stance and the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) monitors global developments very closely.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Whenever potential threats arise, CSA will immediately direct our CII sectors to check for any potential compromise in their networks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SingCERT issues alerts and advisories to the public on actionable steps to take, should they be affected.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the global and transnational nature of such cyber attacks, CSA also works closely with regional CERTs and its international counterparts to track developments and share information.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The attack through the Kaseya VSA is yet another example of how cyber attacks have spilled over into the physical realm, with real-world consequences.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Attackers are clearly learning and evolving their tactics to maximise their gains from a single attack.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We must expect that cyber attacks will become increasingly commonplace and sophisticated.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can strike any of us or our organisations and we must assume that our systems will be breached at some point.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As was mentioned in the response to a query on the SolarWinds attack in Parliament earlier this year, CSA is strengthening its engagements with CII sectors, enterprises and organisations to shift towards a "zero-trust" cybersecurity posture.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This comprises two key principles: first, do not trust any activity on your networks without first verifying it; and second, ensure constant monitoring and vigilance for suspicious activities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Organisations should also implement simple steps not only to prevent breaches, but to detect incidents early and recover quickly from them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These include keeping systems and software updated, backing up data regularly and keeping the back-up offline and practising incident response and business continuity plans to ensure that employees are well-prepared when breaches happen.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government is taking steps to reinforce this mindset and raise the national cybersecurity posture against this new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Businesses and organisations are ultimately responsible for their own cybersecurity and must take action to strengthen their posture.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Conduct an assessment of the risks, consider in advance how you will mitigate them and ensure that you have business continuity plans after an attack.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is in our own interest to stay vigilant against cyber threats, even as we leverage the opportunities of an increasingly digital world.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: That is an increasing threat around the world and while prevention is better than a cure, many companies do end up paying these ransoms in cryptocurrency.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In the Colonial Pipeline case, I think the US government actually worked with the company that was victimised to help them to recover the cryptocurrency that was paid, using law enforcement methods.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I am just wondering whether this is something that the Government can assist companies with, companies who have had to pay ransomware.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I am sure that such support in the systems is something that many companies would also be prepared to pay for, to bear a share of that cost in order to recover the cryptocurrency that is paid.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the first place, prevention is better than cure.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, continued vigilance, I think, is the first line of defence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is a very important point to keep in mind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are there for financial gain and they are not necessarily going to acknowledge the payment of ransoms in order to help you to restore your systems.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the businesses have to consider what their message is to the cyber criminals.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Is your message to them that, well, we have been compromised, we will cough up the ransom as you require?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Or is your message that we have taken preventive measures and, yes, we were affected but we were able to recover and we will strengthen our defences?
